conventions.positive-golden: tests/conformance/<edition>/<name>.cob + <name>.out; the directory selects --std. First line a comment `*> ISO §<clause> <rule> — <what is exercised>`. Unique PROGRAM-ID per program (a stale same-named assembly is served otherwise). Deterministic output only. Do NOT edit any manifest.json — return the entry; the director registers it.
conventions.negative-golden: tests/conformance/negative/<name>.cob + <name>.err (the expected diagnostic substring, e.g. COBOLNET1560). FIRST line of the .cob MUST be `*> reject-at: <year> [<year> ...]`. Do NOT edit the negative manifest — return the entry.
conventions.test-ref-forms: conformance:<edition>/<case> (positive, spec-derived) · conformance:negative/<case> · unit:<Class>.<Method> · conformance-test:<Class>.<Method>. nist:/characterization: and any *_MatchesLegacy method are NOT spec-derived and cannot close a row.
conventions.compiler: src/Cobol.Net.Cli/bin/Debug/net10.0/cobol.exe <file.cob> --std <85|2002|2014|2023> --run  (run in a scratch dir; never dotnet build/test — the tree is shared and a guard refuses builds while a fleet is live).
conventions.citation-check: python scripts/spec/cite.py --check <clause> "<quoted text>"  — every § you cite, no exceptions.

rows.subject: SPECIAL-NAMES paragraph
rows.adjudicator-notes: Rule (SR14 b)4): 'The number of characters specified shall not exceed the number of characters in the native alphanumeric character set.' cite.py --check 12.3.7.3 -> OK §12.3.7.3 14). (The row text's trailing 'c) When the NATIONAL phrase is specified:' is the next sub-item's heading captured by the catalog, not part of this rule.) Enforced by construction, as the code's own remark says: SR14 a) ('A given character shall not be specified more than once in that ALPHABET clause', cite OK §12.3.7.3 14)) is checked in Assign (probe l24_dup `"A" THRU "C" "B"` -> COBOLNET1906 SR14 a), every ordinal is range-checked to the 65,536-unit set, so the specified characters are distinct members of that set and cannot outnumber it. Verified by reading plus the a)/b1 probes; no test pins b4 itself (the SR14 a tests - conformance:negative/pb770-alphabet-duplicate-character - pin the mechanism, not this rule), so test-ref empty. [registrar 14a — editions as adjudicated: 85, 2002, 2014, 2023 (SR14 b)4) | code-location as adjudicated: src/Cobol.Net.Compiler/Binding/DataBinder.Switches.cs#AlphabetLiteralPhrase (Assign - the SR14 a duplicate check)]
rows.rule-text: The number of characters specified shall not exceed the number of characters in the native alphanumeric character set. c) When the NATIONAL phrase is specified:

rows.subject: SPECIAL-NAMES paragraph
rows.adjudicator-notes: SR14 c)4 (cite.py --check 12.3.7.3 'The number of characters specified shall not exceed the number of characters in the native national character set.' -> OK 12.3.7.3 14) 4.). The code has no explicit count test, and none is needed: the native national set is the 65,536 UTF-16 code units (CONFORMANCE DOC-A.1-33; CollatingTable.Repertoire), every operand decodes to a character of that set (the SR14 c1 ordinal range and the c2 class rule in LiteralPhraseOperand), and SR14 a (a character specified more than once -> COBOLNET1906, Assign in AlphabetLiteralPhrase, both arms) refuses any repeat, so no conforming source can specify more than 65,536 characters. probe dir: out/probe/special-names-p2/ (pinned adj-d1 cobol.exe). AL1 `ALPHABET NA FOR NATIONAL IS 1 THRU 65536` (the whole set) compiles and runs; AL2 adds N"A" and draws COBOLNET1906 SR14 a. So the count bound is enforced through SR14 a. No test targets c4 by name (AlphabetLiteralPhraseTests covers c1/c2/c3 and SR14 a on both arms), so test-ref is empty. [registrar 14a — editions as adjudicated: 2002, 2014, 2023 (the NATIONAL phrase and the national character set enter at 2002; Annex E records no 2014->2023 change)]
rows.rule-text: The number of characters specified shall not exceed the number of characters in the native national character set.

rows.subject: SPECIAL-NAMES paragraph
rows.adjudicator-notes: Two rules in one row. (1) SR17 c)5 (cite.py --check 12.3.7.3 'The number of characters specified shall not exceed the number of characters in the native national character set or, when the IN phrase is specified, the number of characters in the character set referenced by alphabet-name-4.' -> OK 17) 5.). The code path is shared with b5: the distinct count is checked against inSet.OrdinalCount under IN. Every national IN set (NATIVE/UTF-16 65,536; UCS-4/UTF-8 1,112,064; a literal-phrase national alphabet, which contains every native character) is at least as large as the 65,536-character native repertoire that members are drawn from, and no national code-name exists (PB793). So c5 cannot be violated by any source, and the check is correctly unconditional on class. (2) SR17 d) (cite.py --check 12.3.7.3 'Alphabet-name-4 shall not reference an alphabet specified with the LOCALE phrase.' -> OK 17) d)) goes through CodedCharacterSetOf. CA5 (alphanumeric LOCALE alphabet) and CA6 (FOR NATIONAL LOCALE alphabet) -> COBOLNET1669 citing 'SR17 d'. No test targets SR17 d or c5 (grep 'SR17 d' in tests: none; the symbolic twin is pb110-symbolic-locale-alphabet), so test-ref is empty. [registrar 14a — editions as adjudicated: 2002, 2014, 2023 (the NATIONAL phrase and the national character set enter at 2002; Annex E records no 2014->2023 change); d) (the LOCALE phrase) likewise 2002+]
rows.rule-text: The number of characters specified shall not exceed the number of characters in the native national character set or, when the IN phrase is specified, the number of characters in the character set referenced by alphabet-name-4. d) Alphabet-name-4 shall not reference an alphabet specified with the LOCALE phrase.

rows.subject: SPECIAL-NAMES paragraph
rows.adjudicator-notes: Rule: 'The words THROUGH and THRU are equivalent.' cite.py --check 12.3.7.3 -> OK §12.3.7.3 12). Both grammar sites accept (THRU | THROUGH) as one alternative; AlphabetLiteralPhrase tests entry.THRU() is not null || entry.THROUGH() is not null, and SwitchBindClass keys on the operand count (lits.Length), never the token. Probes sr12_through / sr12_thru (--std 2023): `ALPHABET AL IS "D" THROUGH "B"` + `CLASS CL IS "0" THROUGH "3"` and the THRU spelling print identical output (A=69 B=3 C=2 D=1 Z=91, V-IN, W-OUT: the descending GR7 k5 run D,C,B at positions 1-3); sr12_through_85 at --std 85 V-IN. Existing goldens use THROUGH in CLASS (conformance:85/pb571_class_condition_one_table) and THRU in ALPHABET (conformance:2002/da1_alphabet_hex_thru) but none pins the EQUIVALENCE (both spellings, same result) on the ALPHABET arm, so test-ref is left empty. [registrar 14a — editions as adjudicated: 85, 2002, 2014, 2023 (the ALPHABET literal-phrase and CLASS THROUGH ranges exist at every edition; Annex E lists no 2014->2023 change)]
rows.rule-text: The words THROUGH and THRU are equivalent.

rows.subject: SPECIAL-NAMES paragraph
rows.adjudicator-notes: Rule: 'When the ALPHABET clause is specified with neither the ALPHANUMERIC phrase nor the NATIONAL phrase, the ALPHANUMERIC phrase is implied.' cite.py --check 12.3.7.3 -> OK §12.3.7.3 13). ForPhraseIsNational returns NATIONAL only when the phrase says so; the unmarked clause takes the alphanumeric branch and the SR14 b-rules. Probes: sr13_implied_nat_lit (`ALPHABET AL IS N"C" N"B"`) and sr13_explicit_nat_lit (`FOR ALPHANUMERIC`) draw the identical COBOLNET1906 SR14 b2 diagnostics; sr13_implied_ok runs as a PCS (C,B,A at positions 1-3); sr13_implied_pcs_nat refuses the implied-alphanumeric alphabet as PROGRAM COLLATING SEQUENCE FOR NATIONAL (COBOLNET0898, §12.3.6.3 SR2) - the implied class is carried downstream, not just to the operand rules. No existing test pins implied == explicit; test-ref empty. [registrar 14a — editions as adjudicated: 2002, 2014, 2023 (the ALPHANUMERIC/NATIONAL phrase enters at 2002; at 85 every alphabet is alphanumeric, which is the same result) | code-location as adjudicated: src/Cobol.Net.Compiler/Binding/DataBinder.Switches.cs#ForPhraseIsNational; src/Cobol.Net.Compiler/Binding/DataBinder.Switches.cs#AlphabetBind (the ALPHANUMERIC branch); src/Cobol.Net.Compiler/Binding/DataBinder.Switches.cs#LiteralPhraseRules.Alphabet]
rows.rule-text: When the ALPHABET clause is specified with neither the ALPHANUMERIC phrase nor the NATIONAL phrase, the ALPHANUMERIC phrase is implied.

rows.subject: SPECIAL-NAMES paragraph
rows.adjudicator-notes: This catalog row LUMPS GR7 d)2 + e + f + g + h + i + j + k (intro, 1a, 1b, 2) - the transcription-indentation artifact kb/Work PB55 (open) owns; each sub-item was checked. d)2 (cite.py --check 12.3.7.4 "If the NATIONAL phrase is specified, the native national coded character set and native national collating sequence are referenced" -> OK): AlphabetBindNational NATIVE -> identity NationalAlphabetDef. e (--check "the collating sequence identified is defined by the locale referenced by locale-name-2 when specified" -> OK): probe/snp3/l22.cob FOR NATIONAL IS LOCALE as national PCS -> N"a" < N"B" (UCA, not code-unit order); l22b.cob LOCALE SWE IS "sv-SE", ALPHABET SV IS LOCALE SWE -> "z" < "o-umlaut" (Swedish tailoring). f/g/h: UCS-4 = coded set + 10646-order sequence (identity on the one-code-unit-per-position substrate; supplementary-plane divergence unreachable per §8.5.1.4, documented DOC-A.1-188); UTF-8/UTF-16 coded sets only - l22c.cob PCS FOR NATIONAL IS a UTF-16 alphabet -> COBOLNET0898 citing Table 6 (golden conformance:2023/l1_alphabet_ucs4_utf8_utf16_correspondence covers the correspondences). i: code-name-1 ASCII/EBCDIC via ImplementorCodeNames (owner decision PB793; DOC-A.1-183 documents set, ordinals, correspondence) - l22.cob SORT ... COLLATING SEQUENCE IS an EBCDIC alphabet orders 'a' < 'B' < '1' (EBCDIC 0x81 < 0xC2 < 0xF1). j: no code-name-2 exists (DOC-A.1-185 vacuous; COBOLNET1907 refuses any). k 1a/1b/2: numeric literal = 1-based native ordinal bounded by the repertoire (SR14 b1/c1 enforced in LiteralPhraseOperand), multi-character literal = successive ascending positions leftmost first, operand order = position order - measured in g9also.cob (ORD("C")=2, ORD("Q")=3, THRU M -> 7). The HIGH-VALUE consequence of an EBCDIC PCS is GR8's finding, not this row's. No single spec-derived test covers the whole lumped row, so test-ref is empty. [registrar 14a — editions as adjudicated: 2002, 2014, 2023 for d)2, e, f, g, h, j (national class and locale facility); 85, 2002, 2014, 2023 for i and k 1-2]
rows.rule-text: If the NATIONAL phrase is specified, the native national coded character set and native national collating sequence are referenced. e) When the LOCALE phrase is specified, the collating sequence identified is defined by the locale referenced by locale-name-2 when specified, otherwise by the locale that is current at the time the collating sequence is used at runtime. When LOCALE is specified in the ALPHANUMERIC phrase, an alphanumeric collating sequence is identified; when specified in the NATIONAL phrase, a national collating sequence is identified. f) When the UCS-4 phrase is specified, the coded character set referenced shall be as specified in ISO/IEC 10646 as UTF-32. Each character of UTF-32 is associated with a corresponding character of the native national character set. The implementor shall specify the correspondence between the characters of UTF-32 and the characters of the native national character set. The collating sequence referenced by the UCS-4 phrase shall be defined by the order in which characters appear in ISO/IEC 10646. g) When the UTF-8 phrase is specified, the coded character set referenced shall be as specified in ISO/IEC 10646 as UTF-8. Each character of ISO/IEC 10646 UTF-32 shall be associated with a corresponding character of the native national character set. The association is the same as the association for the UCS-32 character from which the UTF-8 character was transformed. h) When the UTF-16 phrase is specified, the coded character set referenced shall be as specified in ISO/IEC 10646 as UTF-16. Each character of ISO/IEC 10646 UTF-16 shall be associated with a corresponding character of the native national character set. The association is the same as the association for the UTF-32 character from which the UTF-16 character was transformed. i) When code-name-1 is specified, the alphanumeric coded character set and collating sequence referenced are defined by the implementor. The implementor shall specify the ordinal number of each character for use when code-name-1 references a coded character set and the collating position of each character for use when code-name-1 references a collating sequence. The implementor also shall specify the correspondence between characters of the alphanumeric coded character set specified by code-name-1 and the characters of the native alphanumeric coded character set. The coded character set referenced by code-name-1 is statically defined. j) When code-name-2 is specified, the national coded character set and collating sequence referenced are defined by the implementor. The implementor shall specify the ordinal number of each character for use when code-name-2 references a coded character set and the collating position of each character for use when code-name-2 references a collating sequence. The implementor also shall specify the correspondence between characters of the national coded character set specified by code-name-2 and the characters of the native national coded character set. The coded character set referenced by code-name-2 is statically defined. k) When literal-phrase is specified, the coded character set and collating sequence are defined according to the following rules, where the native coded character set is the type of coded character set or collating sequence being defined, either alphanumeric or national: 1\. The value of each literal specifies: a. The ordinal number of a character within the native character set, if the literal is numeric. This value shall not exceed the value that represents the number of characters in the native character set. b. Otherwise, the actual character within the native character set. If the value of the literal contains multiple characters, each character in the literal, starting with the leftmost character, is assigned successive ascending positions in the collating sequence being specified. 2\. The order in which the literals appear in the ALPHABET clause specifies, in ascending sequence, the ordinal number of the character within the collating sequence being specified.

rows.subject: SPECIAL-NAMES paragraph
rows.adjudicator-notes: Rule: "The implementor shall define the order of characters within the native alphanumeric coded character set and the native national coded character set, associating each character with an ordinal position within the character set." (cite.py --check 12.3.7.4 "The implementor shall define the order of characters within the native alphanumeric coded character set" -> OK §12.3.7.4 6)). The implementation defines it ONCE for both classes: the 65,536 UTF-16 code units in code-unit order, ordinal n = code unit n-1 (CodedCharacterSet doc 'Determinations'; CollatingTable.Repertoire = 0x10000; LiteralPhraseOperand maps a numeric ordinal to (char)(ordinal-1) for either class). Measured with the pinned cobol.exe (probe/snp3/g6n.cob, no PCS): ORD("A")=66, ORD(CHAR(257))=257, ORD(CHAR(65536))=65536 - one consistent association across CHAR/ORD and the ALPHABET/CLASS/SYMBOLIC ordinal readers. The DOCUMENTATION obligation is a separate row: Annex A.1 item 8 ("ALPHABET clause (ordinal number of characters in the native coded character sets). This item is required ... (12.3.7, SPECIAL-NAMES paragraph, General rule 6)") has NO DOC-A.1-8 row in docs/CONFORMANCE.md §7 - owned by the open register note A11 (Annex A.1 documentation register); not re-reported here. Cross-rule observation (NOT this row's defect, reported under GR8/GR10's finding): the native HIGH-VALUE pin (U+00FF, ORD 256) is not the highest ordinal of this 65,536-character native set. No spec-derived covering test (pb59_repertoire_identity pins the implementor's A.1-33 correspondence, not this rule). [registrar 14a — editions as adjudicated: 85, 2002, 2014, 2023 (the native NATIONAL half from 2002, with the national class)]
rows.rule-text: The implementor shall define the order of characters within the native alphanumeric coded character set and the native national coded character set, associating each character with an ordinal position within the character set.

rows.subject: SPECIAL-NAMES paragraph, ALPHABET clause (coded character set referenced by STANDARD-2 phrase)
rows.adjudicator-notes: cite.py --check 12.3.7.4 'the implementor shall specify whether the International Reference Version or a national version is referenced' -> OK §12.3.7.4 7) c). Read CollatingModel.CodedCharacterSet (OrdinalCount STANDARD-1/STANDARD-2 => 128; Medium identity; identity alphabet for PCS) and CobolClass.CodedSetKind.Ascii (128-char membership). No code path selects a national ISO 646 variant. Probe probe/p182/s2.cob at --std 85 and 2023: AB~ IS S2 true, é IS S2 false, ORD('A')=66, a>B, é>~ under PCS S2. No spec-derived test uses STANDARD-2 (pb695 names it only as an optional-word syntax check), so Pinned by is empty. Owning note: kb/Work/PB1534, PB1535.
rows.rule-text: SPECIAL-NAMES paragraph, ALPHABET clause (coded character set referenced by STANDARD-2 phrase). This item is required. This item shall be documented in the implementor's user documentation. (12.3.7, SPECIAL-NAMES paragraph, General rule 7c)

rows.subject: SPECIAL-NAMES paragraph, ALPHABET clause, literal phrase (ordinal number of characters not specified)
rows.adjudicator-notes: cite.py --check 12.3.7.4 'the implementor defines the ordinal number within the character code set being specified for each character within the native character set that is not specified by the literal-1 phrase' -> OK §12.3.7.4 7) (k 4.). Read CollatingModel.CodedCharacterSet.CharAt (ordinal <= NextFree -> RepByPos; else the want-th unspecified code unit in native order) and OrdinalCount (65536 for a literal-phrase set). Probe probe/p186/k4.cob at --std 85 and 2023: S1=Z S2=Y S3=X S4=00 S5=01 S70=B; CLASS 1 THRU 3 IN AL excludes W (native contiguous X..Z, GR12) — consistent. kb/Work/PB1092 (open, process_only, claims DOC-A.1-186) owes exactly this row; integrator must also correct docs/CONFORMANCE.md §2 row 27's sentence 'GR7 k4 leaves that correspondence to the implementor and this one does not define it' (PB1092's second deliverable). No spec-derived test pins the scheme. Owning note: kb/Work/PB1092. REFUTER: headline 'collating position plus one' corrected (spec positions are 1-based, so 'plus one' read as an off-by-one; the code's '+1' is over 0-based positions); added the ALSO-reduced upper bound, probed refute-probe/p186/o.cob: ordinals 65534/65535 -> U+FFFE/U+FFFF, 65536 -> COBOLNET1670. k4.cob re-run at 85/2002/2014/2023 identical.
rows.rule-text: SPECIAL-NAMES paragraph, ALPHABET clause, literal phrase (ordinal number of characters not specified). This item is required. The implementor shall document the scheme used for assigning the ordinal number, but does not need to specify the ordinal number character-by-character. (12.3.7, SPECIAL-NAMES paragraph General rule 7k4)

rows.subject: STOP statement
rows.adjudicator-notes: cite.py --check 14.9.42.4 GR6 -> OK. STOP RUN throws StopRun, caught only at the generated Main's 'catch (StopRun) { }' (searched src/Cobol.Net.Runtime and CodeGen for generic catch clauses: only ProbeSiblingModule's catch-all, which wraps assembly loading, not activation). Probes: p1..p9 never print 'AFTER'; q1 terminates from a CALLed program inside an inline PERFORM - neither 'SUB-AFTER' nor 'MAIN-AFTER-CALL' runs. Doc defect only: StopRun.cs summary cites 'ISO §14.9.43' - that is the STRING statement; it should be §14.9.42.4 GR6. No spec-derived test asserts termination from call depth -> test-ref empty. [editions as adjudicated: 1985, 2002, 2014, 2023 (STOP RUN is in every edition; §14.9.42 of the 2023 text)]
rows.rule-text: Execution of the run unit terminates and control is transferred to the operating system.
